title: Fundamentals
description: Start with values, variables, strings, numbers, input, and output.

lessons.title: First steps
lessons.content:
A variable gives a value a name. Python can store text, whole numbers, and decimal numbers.

Example:
name = "Ada"
age = 12
print(f"Hello, {name}! Next year you will be {age + 1}.")

The f before a string lets you put expressions inside braces.
lessons.exercise:
1. Store your name and favorite hobby in variables and print a sentence.
2. Convert a distance from kilometers to miles (multiply by 0.621371).
3. Ask for a temperature in Celsius and print its Fahrenheit conversion.

title: Decisions and loops
description: Make choices with conditions and repeat work with loops.

lessons.title: Choose and repeat
lessons.exercise:
1. Ask for an age and label the person as a child, teen, or adult.
2. Print numbers from 1 to 20 and label each even or odd.
3. Make a number guessing game with a fixed secret number.

title: Collections
description: Group related data with lists, dictionaries, sets, and tuples.

lessons.title: Grouping data
lessons.content:
Lists keep an ordered collection. Dictionaries associate keys with values. Sets keep unique values.

Example:
shopping = ["apples", "bread"]
shopping.append("tea")
scores = {"Ari": 8, "Bo": 10}
print(shopping)
print(scores["Ari"])
lessons.exercise:
1. Make a shopping list, add and remove an item, then print each item.
2. Make a dictionary of names and phone numbers.
3. Count how often each word appears in a sentence.

title: Functions
description: Give reusable behavior a name and split problems into smaller steps.

lessons.title: Reusable behavior
lessons.content:
Functions accept inputs through parameters and can send a result back with return.

Example:
def rectangle_area(width, height):
    return width * height

area = rectangle_area(4, 3)
print(area)
lessons.exercise:
1. Write a function that converts Celsius to Fahrenheit.
2. Write a function that returns the average of a list of numbers.
3. Split your guessing game into small functions with clear names.

title: Modules and errors
description: Reuse the standard library and handle invalid input clearly.

lessons.title: Imports and input validation
lessons.content:
An import gives you access to code from another module. Use try and except for errors you expect and know how to handle.

Example:
import random

print(random.randint(1, 6))

try:
    age = int(input("Age: "))
except ValueError:
    print("Please enter a whole number.")
lessons.exercise:
1. Import math and calculate a circle's area.
2. Keep asking until the user enters a valid whole number.
3. Put a function in a separate file and import it.

title: Files and data
description: Read and write files, and save structured information as JSON or CSV.

lessons.title: Save and load data
lessons.content:
Pathlib provides convenient file paths. The json module converts between Python data and JSON text.

Example:
import json
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("progress.json")
path.write_text(json.dumps({"done": True}))
data = json.loads(path.read_text())
print(data)
lessons.exercise:
1. Write a note to a text file, then read it back.
2. Save a list of completed lessons as JSON.
3. Read a CSV file with Python's csv module and summarize a column.

title: Object-oriented Python
description: Model related data and behavior with classes and instances.

lessons.title: Classes and instances
lessons.exercise:
1. Add a method that describes a book.
2. Create a Library class that stores books and finds one by title.
3. Prevent a checked-out book from being checked out again.

title: Testing
description: Check that your program behaves as expected with repeatable tests.

lessons.title: Test your code
lessons.content:
A test calls your code with known inputs and checks the result. Python includes unittest in its standard library.

Example:
import unittest

class AreaTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_rectangle(self):
        self.assertEqual(4 * 3, 12)

Run tests with: python -m unittest
lessons.exercise:
1. Write tests for a temperature conversion function.
2. Test your shopping-list or guessing-game behavior.
3. Make one test fail by changing the code, then restore the correct behavior.
